messages:
ioanna: FYI customer Connor seeing intermittent 502/524 spikes hitting hosted API after our cert swap at ~09:12 UTC. They repro with short curl loop and we see TLS handshake failures in gateway logs.

mike_oncall: can you paste the curl + error? and which customer endpoint?

ioanna: curl loop:
```
for i in {1..50}; do curl -vvv -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' https://api.hosted.redwood.ai/v1/generate || true; sleep 0.2; done
```
Responses: several `* Connection #X to host api.hosted.redwood.ai left intact` then `* Closing connection 0` and finally `HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway` or connection reset.

ioanna: customer: connor@acme-inc, endpoint: /v1/generate model=redwood-3-small, region=us-west-2. They reported after cert rotation completed.

jules_sre: logs look like TLS handshake timeout before SNI selected on a fraction of connections. @dns-bot any resolver events at that time?

 dns-bot: Automated note: between 09:10-09:20 UTC we had increased NXDOMAIN retries to one of our upstreams (isp-2) and a short 45s period of EDNS0 truncation fallback to TCP for resolver pop-us-west-2. Affected queries: api.hosted.redwood.ai A records.

andrew_eng: that could produce stale IPs if cache fallback path mis-ordered. any TTL changes in the cert swap runbook (we lowered origin CNAME TTL to 30s then restored to 300s)?

ioanna: yes TTL was 30s during swap. hypothesis: some resolvers hit old edge IP that still had previous cert chain leading to SNI mismatch/cert-rotation connection aborts and gateway returned 502. Customer saw spikes while resolver rebinds.

mike_oncall: repro attempt: run curl with `--resolve` to force IPs and compare. also can we get tcpdump from the edge to see SNI vs cert presented?

ioanna: sent request to customer to run two quick checks:
1) `curl -v https://api.hosted.redwood.ai/v1/generate --resolve api.hosted.redwood.ai:443:34.56.78.90` (forced old IP)
2) `curl -v https://api.hosted.redwood.ai/v1/generate --resolve api.hosted.redwood.ai:443:52.11.22.33` (forced new IP)

connor_customer: ran both. old IP -> TLS alert, handshake aborted. new IP -> 200 OK consistently. attaching raw curl logs.

ioanna: thanks Connor, that nails it. looks resolver race + low TTL + upstream truncation caused clients to hit mixed IP fleet mid-rotation.

jules_sre: short-term mitigation: roll back TTL to 300s globally? might be too late. we should ensure edge serves consistent chain across IPs ASAP. @andrew_eng can you verify cert propagated to all edge hosts and confirm chain order?

andrew_eng: starting cert propagation check now. initial scan shows ~2% of edge instances still reporting old cert chain due to failed reload on ctrlplane push. kicking a targeted reload on those hosts.

deploy-bot: deploy/edge-cert-reload triggered for hosts [edge-17, edge-23, edge-98] by andrew_eng. ETA ~90s.

mike_oncall: once reloads finish, let's ask Connor to re-run curl loop. If still flaky we'll temporarily increase TTL and open a ticket with upstream resolver for EDNS0 truncation.

ioanna: agreed. Connor, can you run the same 50x loop in ~2m and paste results?

connor_customer: running now, 0/50 were 5xx. Looks stable. Thanks team. :tada:

jules_sre: follow-ups:
- postmortem to include root cause: resolver TCP fallback + low swap TTL + incomplete cert reload on subset of edge hosts.
- action items: increase pre-swap TTL guidance to 300s minimum, add verification step to cert-swap runbook to confirm cert on all active edge IPs, add alert when resolver upstream returns truncation spikes.

ioanna: filing a support ticket with those notes and scheduling postmortem with eng and dns teams. Closing thread when postmortem created. :white_check_mark:
